title: BNY首席经济学家解析美联储利率路径与日本央行政策正常化
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Before we get to the decision tomorrow, I do want to go back to kind of the battle days, if you will, of that sort of thing.
segments.zh: 在明天做出决定之前，我想先回顾一下当年的艰难时期。

segments.en: Remain is this is where you want me to make my apology, because we did write those papers, but we did not include sections on risks
segments.zh: 这里需要我道歉，因为我们确实写了那些论文，但没有包含政策风险以及如何退出的部分。

segments.en: to the policy and how to exit. Okay.
And I think in retrospect, there are risks and in particular, it's hard to get out once you're in.
segments.zh: 回想起来，确实存在风险，尤其是一旦进入就很难退出。

segments.en: Well, let's talk about the exit. I mean, they finally came out of it in early 2024.
segments.zh: 我们来谈谈退出。他们在2024年初终于走出了负利率。

segments.en: I mean, they're still only in the 1% range, but that's a huge turnaround.
segments.zh: 目前利率仍只在1%区间，但已经是巨大的转变。

segments.en: As you sort of grade the progress that they've made, particularly on the monetary policy side, do you think that what has happened so far
segments.zh: 评估他们取得的进展，特别是在货币政策方面，你认为迄今为止

segments.en: in this two and a half years since they came out of the negative rates has been, if not a success, certainly constructive?
segments.zh: 自退出负利率以来的两年半里，这些进展即使不算成功，也无疑是建设性的？

segments.en: It's enormous progress, because you have to put the central bank within society at large.
segments.zh: 这是巨大的进步，因为必须把央行放在整个社会背景中来看。

segments.en: And Japan is leading the pack for most macroeconomic distinctions, so that is an ageing population.
segments.zh: 日本在大多数宏观经济特征上都走在前面，比如人口老龄化。

segments.en: And for an ageing population, low inflation or deflation isn't such a bad thing because it's transfer an income from the young to the old.
segments.zh: 对老龄化人口来说，低通胀或通缩并非坏事，因为它将收入从年轻人转移给老年人。

segments.en: It's not an accident that they lived so long without.
segments.zh: 他们能长期如此并非偶然。
